thread:
maria-ux: quick question — for the permissions console: how should we show bindings for 'guest principals' (external service accounts / cross-tenant identities)? UX is getting messy when a role maps both to a tenant user and an external principal in the same binding.
kevin-p: adding context: security wants explicit separation. "guest principal" != normal user. We need clear affordance and auditability. cc @sneh for platform constraints.
sneh: we currently store bindings as {subject_type, subject_id, scope}. frontend just lists them. supporting two subject_types is easy, but the tricky part is scoping semantics (inherit vs isolated).
maria-ux: want to propose two visual approaches: 1) split list into "Internal users & service accounts" and "External/Guest principals" 2) show a badge on each row with a tooltip explaining access boundary. Opinions?
olivia-product: +1 on separation. Also add a short inline to explain "why guest principals exist" for enterprise admins. They keep asking on-support.
eva-plat: fwiw, routing policies + quotas depend on resolved tenant id. If guest principals are allowed to cross-tenant, we need to block certain model routes by default. That ties into rollout policies.
kevin-p: important: default deny for guest principals for high-risk routes, ability to opt-in at role binding level. UI needs a toggle: "allow guest principal access to restricted routes" with an alert.
maria-ux: design question: should we let admins attach route-level exceptions to a role-binding? i.e. Role X bound to GuestPrincipal Y, plus a per-binding exceptions list.
sneh: backend can support per-binding exceptions, but it increases evaluation cost on request path. We can cache effective permissions per (subject, scope) but invalidation becomes hairy.
olivia-product: maybe avoid per-binding exceptions. Instead allow per-scope policy (scope-level routing policy) + an overrides table for a few trusted principals managed via a separate flow.
kevin-p: UX should make escalation explicit. If someone toggles allow on a guest principal, surface the audit checklist: last-used, originating tenant, expires_at.
maria-ux: mockup idea: two-line row

```
Guest: acme-external-service
Role: ReadOnly
Scope: Tenant:acme-prod  [badge: GUEST]
[Allow restricted routes?] [Expires: 2026-12-01]
```

hover -> shows origin tenant, identity provider, last auth time.
sneh: sounds fine. We should also ensure the API expresses subject provenance. Current API only returns "subject_id" which isn't enough. Need `subject_provenance` and `issuer`.
eva-plat: agree. And add telemetry: tag every evaluation with `principal_type=guest|internal` so we can measure failures and SLO impacts.
olivia-product: also need a migration story for existing bindings that implicitly include guest principals (we have a few created by onboarding scripts). A bulk review UI would help.
kevin-p: ops-bot can kick off a bulk-review job if we create an internal flag.
ops-bot: created ticket INF-3215: "Guest principal binding review job" assigned to @sneh. ETA 2w.
sneh: thanks. I'll prototype an API change: add `provenance` to binding payload and a query param `include_provenance=true` for listing to keep compatibility.
maria-ux: next steps for UI: i'll produce two quick mocks (split list and badges) and a microcopy doc explaining terms (guest, service account, external). i'll post in #design-review later today.
olivia-product: one more ask — show an "impact preview" when toggling allow (estimated affected routes + sample tokens). not required for MVP but high priority for enterprise.
kevin-p: let's keep MVP minimal: separate section + badge + toggle with audit modal. Track telemetry events: toggle_click, allow_explicit, migration_review_started.
maria-ux: perfect. thanks everyone. I'll link mocks + copy here when ready. :thumbsup:
